46.title: Chairman Capito Asks Army Corps Leaders about WRDA Implementation, Project Cost Overruns
46.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to conduct oversight of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) with Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, Adam Telle, and the 56th Chief of Engineers and Commanding General, Lieutenant General William H. Graham, Jr.

During the hearing, Chairman Capito questioned the Assistant Secretary Telle and Lieutenant General Graham about the delayed implementation of provisions included in prior Water Resource Development Act (WRDA)s, and cost overrun issues on projects.

47.title: Chairman Capito Leads Oversight Hearing of U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
47.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to conduct oversight of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps) with Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, Adam Telle, and the 56th Chief of Engineers and Commanding General, Lieutenant General William H. Graham, Jr.

In her opening statement, Chairman Capito highlighted several ongoing studies and projects in West Virginia authorized by prior Water Resources Development Act (WRDA)s, and the importance of the Corps’ work to address water resources challenges across the nation.

48.title: Capito Asks about Use of Prescribed Burns for Forest Management, Alternative Shipping Fuel Options
48.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to examine a discussion draft of the Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act (WEPA); and S. 881, the Renewable Fuel for Ocean-Going Vessels Act.

During the hearing, Chairman Capito questioned witnesses about the need for states expand the use of prescribed burns, and the complexities surrounding prescribed burns and exceptional events under current law. Additionally, Chairman Capito ask about the future of alternative fuels for shipping.

49.title: Chairman Capito Leads Legislative Hearing to Discuss Wildfire, Biofuel Legislation
49.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to examine a discussion draft of the Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act (WEPA); and S. 881, the Renewable Fuel for Ocean-Going Vessels Act.

In her opening statement, Chairman Capito detailed how WEPA would ease barriers for states to manage their forests, reduce wildfire risk, and protect human health and the environment through prescribed burns. Additionally, she thanked Senator Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) for his leadership in introducing the Renewable Fuel for Ocean-Going Vessels Act ahead of a discussion on alternative fuels in shipping as part of today’s hearing.

50.title: Capito Questions NRC Commissioners on Revised Mission Statement, Opportunities for Efficiency
50.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to conduct oversight of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) with the current Chairman and Commissioners of the NRC.

During the hearing, Chairman Capito questioned the NRC Commissioners on steps that could be taken to make their updated mission statement actionable, and how reporting requirements can be streamlined to create efficiency.

51.title: Capito Leads NRC Oversight Hearing, Urges Further Improvement, efficiency from the Commission
51.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing to conduct oversight of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) with the current Chairman and Commissioners of the NRC.

In her opening statement, Chairman Capito emphasized the importance of implementing the ADVANCE Act, and how President Trump’s executive orders complement efforts to streamline processes at the NRC to rapidly deploy nuclear energy. Additionally, Chairman Capito highlighted the importance of NRC maintaining their central role of ensuring nuclear safety while improving their policy and licensing to create efficiency and meet the current moment for nuclear energy.

52.title: EPW Favorably Reports Katherine Scarlett to lead CEQ, Approves GSA Resolutions
52.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a business meeting to consider the nomination of Katherine Scarlett to be a Member of the Council on Environmental Quality, and 10 Committee Resolutions to approve prospectuses from the General Services Administration.

Scarlett’s nomination was favorably reported by the EPW Committee, and the GSA resolutions were approved by voice vote. The nomination now heads to the full U.S. Senate for consideration.

53.title: Chairman Capito Delivers Floor Speech on Need for Bipartisan Permitting Reform Legislation
53.description: Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, delivered remarks on Senate Floor outlining the need for comprehensive, bipartisan reforms to our nation’s environmental review and permitting processes.

54.title: Chairman Capito: “David Wright Meets that Mark” to Lead Nuclear Regulatory Commission
54.description:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, spoke on Senate Floor in support of David Wright’s confirmation to serve as a member of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

Throughout the confirmation process, Chairman Capito has highlighted the experience and leadership that David Wright brings to the NRC during a crucial moment for nuclear energy in America. As directed by Chairman Capito’s ADVANCE Act that was signed into law last July, Chairman Wright was central in crafting NRC’s updated mission statement and supports ongoing efforts to enable the deployment of new nuclear more efficiently, predictably, and safely.

55.title: Chairman Capito Participates in EPW T&I Subcommittee Hearing on Surface Transportation Improvements
55.description: Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, participated in an EPW Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee hearing on proposals to improve America’s transportation infrastructure.

56.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on the nominations of Katherine Scarlett to be a Member of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and Jeffrey Hall to be an Assistant Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). 

In her questioning, Chairman Capito highlighted the qualifications of the nominees, and asked about implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and prioritizing the cleanup of Superfund sites.

57.title: Chairman Capito Opening Statement at Hearing to Consider Scarlett, Hall Nominations
57.description: Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on the nominations of Katherine Scarlett to be a Member of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and Jeffrey Hall to be an Assistant Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

58.title: Chairman Capito Highlights Surface Transportation Priorities from Stakeholder Experiences
58.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on constructing the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Bill with stakeholders’ perspectives.

During her questions, Chairman Capito asked about the role of the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Bill regarding economic development, and how permitting reform remains key in the efficient development of our country’s surface transportation network.

59.title: Chairman Capito Outlines Principles for Crafting the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Bill
59.description: Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on constructing the Surface Transportation Reauthorization Bill with stakeholders’ perspectives. In her opening remarks, Chairman Capito reiterated her three principles for crafting this legislation, and how developing a bipartisan proposal in the Senate remains a central priority for the EPW Committee.

66.title: Chairman Capito Opening Statement at Hearing on EPA’s Proposed FY26 Budget with Administrator Zeldin
66.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) proposed budget for Fiscal Year 2026 with EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin.

In her opening remarks, Chairman Capito applauded Administrator Zeldin for his leadership in returning EPA to its core mission, reversing the federal overreach of the previous administration, and focusing the agency on issues important to West Virginia and the country. Additionally, Chairman Capito highlighted ways EPA’s proposed budget benefits hardworking Americans and areas it can be improved.

67.title: Chairman Capito Talks California Waiver CRA at GOP Leadership Stakeout

68.title: Chairman Capito Asks Nominees About Bridge Funding, PFAS Remediation, USACE Project Prioritization
68.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on the nominations of Sean McMaster to be Administrator of the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), John Busterud to be Assistant Administrator for the Office of Solid Waste of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and Adam Telle to be Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works. 

During the hearing, Chairman Capito questioned the nominees about initiatives to support our nation’s bridges through FHWA policy and funding, the importance of federal efforts to address PFAS contamination, and promptly addressing priority projects through the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE).

70.title: Capito Remarks in Favor of CRA Eliminating Biden Rule Prohibiting Reclassification of Major Sources

71.title: Capito Asks Water Infrastructure Leaders about Challenges in Rural Communities, IIJA Implementation
71.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing examining successes from water infrastructure policies and provisions in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). This hearing serves as the foundation for the EPW Committee’s work to craft bipartisan legislation to reauthorize water infrastructure programs ahead of their expiration next year. 

In her questions, Chairman Capito asked water infrastructure stakeholders about water infrastructure challenges facing rural communities and potential solutions, as well as the implementation of water provisions in the IIJA.

72.title: Chairman Capito Leads Hearing Examining Water Infrastructure Successes from IIJA
72.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing examining successes from water infrastructure policies and provisions in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA). This hearing serves as the foundation for the EPW Committee’s work to craft bipartisan legislation to reauthorize water infrastructure programs ahead of their expiration next year. 

In her opening remarks, Chairman Capito outlined her principles for this reauthorization effort, centered on policies that enhance rural and underserved communities’ ability to deliver water projects, strengthen cooperative federalism, and deliver outcomes that prioritize safe water and reliable infrastructure.

73.title: Chairman Capito Questions at Hearing on Superfund Program Improvements
73.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on identifying improvements to the future management of the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Superfund Program. 

In her questioning, Chairman Capito asked about particular factors that contribute to delays and increase costs of Superfund cleanups, and what actions can be taken from state and volunteer efforts to provide certainty for impacted communities. Additionally, Chairman Capito highlighted the bipartisan agreement to make meaningful improvements to the Superfund program.

74.title: Chairman Capito Opening Statement on Needed Improvement to EPA’s Superfund Program
74.description:
Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led a hearing on identifying improvements to the future management of the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Superfund Program.

171.title: EPW Committee Advances Bipartisan Nuclear Energy Bill from Capito, Carper, Whitehouse
171.description:
Today, the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee passed legislation introduced by Ranking Member Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman Tom Carper (D-Del.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), and a bipartisan group of their colleagues that would help position the United States as the undisputed international leader for nuclear energy technologies.

The Accelerating Deployment of Versatile, Advanced Nuclear for Clean Energy (ADVANCE) Act of 2023, which Capito led introduction of in March, passed out of the EPW Committee by a vote of 16-3.

“From both a national security and energy independence standpoint, America has everything to gain from being the world’s leader in nuclear energy, and today we took an important step forward in achieving that goal,” Ranking Member Capito said. “This legislation gives a major boost to a clean, reliable power generation source, and provides the tools needed for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to facilitate the development and deployment of new technologies here in the United States. I’m proud of the work that went into the ADVANCE Act and that the EPW Committee continues to demonstrate we can successfully collaborate in addressing critical issues like nuclear energy in a bipartisan way.”

191.title: Capito Speaks Prior to Senate Passing Her Resolution Blocking Biden’s Waters of the US (WOTUS) Rule
191.description:
Today, the U.S. Senate passed Senator Shelley Moore Capito’s (R-W.Va.) Congressional Review Act (CRA) joint resolution of disapproval that overturns President Biden’s overreaching Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule by a vote of 53-43.

Senator Capito, the Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, led her colleagues in introducing the resolution in February 2023 after the Biden administration announced a new rule in December 2022 repealing the Navigable Waters Protection Rule (NWPR), and changing the definition of Waters of the United States in a way that will significantly expand federal regulatory authority. 

“By voting to overturn President Biden’s waters rule, we are sending a clear, bipartisan message that Congress, even a divided one, will defend working Americans in the face of executive overreach,” Ranking Member Capito said. “I’m proud to lead my colleagues in standing up for farmers and ranchers, landowners and builders, and energy and infrastructure workers across the United States. I urge President Biden not to overrule the will of a bipartisan majority in Congress, and instead draft a new rule that doesn’t unfairly penalize millions of Americans and jeopardize future growth in our country.”

607.title: EPW Committee Passes Bipartisan WILD Act for Wildlife Conservation
607.description:
U.S. Senator John Barrasso (R-WY), chairman of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), delivered the following remarks at a committee business meeting to consider S. 826, the Wildlife Innovation and Longevity Driver (WILD) Act. The bipartisan WILD Act passed the committee by voice vote. 

The WILD Act was introduced by Chairman John Barrasso (R-WY) and is cosponsored by committee ranking member Sen. Tom Carper (D-DE) and Sens. Jim Inhofe (R-OK), Cory Booker (D-NJ), John Boozman (R-AK), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI). The legislation has also received support from World Wildlife Fund and the Family Farm Alliance.

The WILD Act will promote wildlife conservation, assist in the management of invasive species, and help protect endangered species. The bipartisan legislation will reauthorize government conservation programs. It will also establish prize competitions to prevent illegal poaching and trafficking, manage invasive species, promote conservation, and protect endangered wildlife.

In addition, the EPW Committee also passed by voice vote: S. 518, the Small and Rural Community Clean Water Technical Assistance Act; S. 692, the Water Infrastructure Flexibility Act of 2017; and S. 675, the Long Island Sound Restoration and Stewardship Act.

(April 5, 2017)

145.description: After 24 years of service on the Environment and Public Works Committee, Senators and members of the Administration thank Chairman Tom Carper (D-Del.) for his tenure as a unifying leader and an environmental champion.

146.title: Senator Carper Urges Senate Passage of the Water Resources Development Act of 2024
146.description: U.S. Senator Tom Carper (D-Del.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, speaks on the Senate floor urging his colleagues to pass the Water Resources Development Act of 2024 (WRDA 24). The Water Resources Development Act is biennial legislation that authorizes flood control, navigation and ecosystem restoration projects for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (Corps). WRDA 2024 authorizes water infrastructure projects and programs that will impact all 50 states, including more than 200 feasibility studies and 21 new or modified construction projects. The bill includes provisions to help address significant unobligated balances under the Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) program. 393.description: On Thursday, July 13th at 10:00 a.m., U.S. Senators Tom Carper, (D-Del.), top Democrat on the Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, Debbie Stabenow (D-Mich.), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition and Forestry, Ben Cardin (D-Md.), ranking member of the EPW Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure, Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), ranking member of the EPW Subcommittee on Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife and Cory Booker (D-N.J) co-hosted a roundtable entitled, “Drinking Water: A Crisis in Every State.” The panel provided an opportunity to hear from drinking water experts on contamination in our nation’s drinking water infrastructure and to review funding priorities leading up to a larger infrastructure debate that is facing the United States Senate.

394.title: Senator Carper Calls for Bipartisan Support for Kristine Svinicki to Continue As NRC Chairman

396.description: On May 24, 2017, Senator Tom Carper (D-Del.), top Democrat on the Environment and Public Works Committee, took to the Senate floor to urge President Trump to uphold our commitments and stay in the Paris Agreement.

397.title: Senators Carper and Whitehouse Host Coastal Infrastructure Roundtable
397.description: On Thursday, May 11th at 10:30 a.m., U.S. Senators Tom Carper, (D-Del.), top Democrat on the Environment and Public Works Committee, and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) held a public roundtable to highlight the current state of coastal infrastructure, examine the changing environmental conditions for which coastal communities must prepare, and discuss the federal government’s role in assisting states, tribes and localities in meeting coastal infrastructure needs.

398.title: Ranking Member Carper, Senate Democrats Host Panel Discussion on Pruitt Nomination
398.description: U.S. Senator Tom Carper, (D-Del.), top Democrat on the Environment and Public Works Committee, will host a panel discussion with Senate Democrats, as well as national and state leaders, to further examine Mr. Pruitt’s record and highlight the qualifications needed to lead the agency.

399.title: Ranking Member Carper, EPW Democrats Call for an EPA Guided by Science
399.description: On January 12, 2017, U.S. Senator Tom Carper, (D-Del.), top Democrat on the Environment and Public Works Committee, was joined by fellow committee Democrats as well as conservationists, medical professionals, scientists and concerned citizens to highlight the importance of continuing to have an EPA guided by sound science and able to protect the health of the American people.

400.title: Sen. Boxer speaks on Senate Floor About Republicans’ Failure to Help People of Flint, MI in CR
400.description: Senator Barbara Boxer spoke on the floor regarding the Republican CR’s exclusion of funding to help solve the water crisis in Flint, Michigan.

401.title: Senator Barbara Boxer speaks on Senate Floor on the Water Resources Development Act of 2016
401.description: Senator Barbara Boxer spoke on the floor on the Water Resources Development Act of 2016.

402.title: Senator Barbara Boxer speaks on the Senate Floor Exposing Web of Denial Blocking Action on Climate
402.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor regarding climate science.

403.title: Boxer Welcomes Orange County Official at Hearing on Innovative Water Technologies
403.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, was so pleased to welcome Denis Bilodeau of the Orange County Water District as a witness at today’s Committee hearing focused on innovative water supply technologies.

404.title: Boxer Urges Colleagues to Oppose Anti-Safety, Special Interest Provision in House FAA Bill
404.description: Senator Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke in opposition to a dangerous provision in the House FAA Bill. The provision would restrict states the right to pass laws preventing truck drivers from being docked for bathroom breaks, meals breaks and "non-driving" responsibilities, such as loading the truck.

405.title: Boxer Opposes CRA Resolutions That Would Undermine Clean Air Act and Clean Power Plant
405.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor urging colleagues to vote against S.J. Res. 23 and S. J. Res. 24, which respectively block carbon pollution standards for new, modified and reconstructed power plants, and the President’s Clean Power Plan for existing power plants. The resolutions also prohibit the Environmental Protection Agency from undertaking similar rulemaking to address carbon pollution, and Republicans have yet to produce an alternative plan of their own. The Clean Power Plan is projected to cut emissions from existing power plants 32% below 2012 levels by 2030, produce many public health and economic benefits, and contribute towards our nation’s leadership in tackling global climate change.

406.title: Boxer Speaks in Opposition to S. 1140
406.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke in opposition to S. 1140 which rolls back critical protections for small streams and wetlands that provide drinking water to 1 in 3 Americans or 117 million people.

407.title: Boxer Speaks On Senate Floor Regarding Transportation Legislation and PTC Delay
407.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, stated on the Senate floor that it is time for the House and Senate to get to conference so a long-term transportation bill can be implemented without further delay.  Senator Boxer also emphasized the need to ensure Positive Train Control is implemented properly within the new time frame.

408.title: Boxer Speaks on the Floor About The Need For The House To Pass a Long-Term Transportation Bill
408.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor to urge the House of Representatives to pass a robust, multi-year surface transportation bill. The current authorization for our surface transportation programs expires October 29th.

409.title: Boxer's Opening Statement for Business Meeting on S. 1324, S. 1500 and other legislation
409.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member, made the following remarks during an Environment and Public Works Committee markup of several bills, including S. 1324 and S. 1500, which are extremely harmful to public health.  S. 1324 would block the President’s Clean Power Plan and allow states to opt out of complying with any future plan.  S. 1500 would end the requirement that a Clean Water Act permit is needed for spraying dangerous pesticides into a body of water.

410.title: Senators Boxer, Schumer, Whitehouse and Schatz go to Floor to Ask #WhatsTheGOPClimatePlan?
410.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Brian Schatz (D-HI), and Edward Markey (D-MA) took part in a colloquy on the Senate floor to talk about the the importance of Obama Administration's Clean Power Plan. against Republican attacks. The Senators posed a question to Republicans who oppose President Obama's Clean Power Plan -- President Obama's Clean Power Plan -- #WhatsTheGOPClimatePlan?

411.title: Senators Boxer and Inhofe Praise Final Passage of the DRIVE Act
411.description: U.S. Senators Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, and Jim Inhofe (R-Okla.), Chairman of the EPW Committee, today praised passage of H.R. 22, the Developing a Reliable and Innovative Vision for the Economy Act (DRIVE Act) in a vote of 65 to 34.

412.title: Senator Boxer:  Where is the House’s Transportation Bill?
412.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor to respond to comments made by House Republican leadership about the transportation bill. The Highway Trust Fund expires this Friday, July 31st.

413.title: Senators Boxer, Reid, Whitehouse, Schatz, and Markey Participate in a Colloquy on Climate Change
413.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, Democratic Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Brian Schatz (D-HI), and Edward Markey (D-MA) spoke on the Senate floor to urge Congress to act on climate change. The Senators stated that that the denial of climate change must end and Congress has to act before the consequences are too severe. Follow/use the hashtag #WhatstheGOPClimatePlan on twitter.

414.title: Boxer, Inhofe and Klobuchar Speaks on the Importance of Guaranteed Long-Term Infrastructure Funding
414.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, Jim Inhofe (R-OK), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, and Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), spoke on the urgent need for guaranteed long-term funding for America's transportation system. Boxer highlighted some of the 60,000 bridges that are structurally deficient. The highway bill being considered on the Senate floor would provide three years of guaranteed funding and six years of program authorization. The Highway Trust Fund expires this Friday, July 31st.

415.title: Boxer Speaks on the Need to Fix Functionally Obsolete Bridges through a Long-Term Highway Bill
415.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the importance of strengthening our infrastructure through fixing functionally obsolete bridges. The current highway bill on the Senate floor would provide three years of guaranteed funding and six years of program authorization. The Highway Trust Fund expires this Friday, July 31st.

416.title: Boxer Calls on Colleagues to Support Bipartisan, Long-term Transportation Bill
416.description: In an unusual Sunday session, Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke about the importance of moving forward on a long-term transportation bill. The majority of states rely on the federal government for transportation funding, and countless infrastructure projects and jobs across the country could be jeopardized if the Highway Trust Fund expires on July 31st.

417.title: Boxer Stresses the Need to Move Forward on a Long-Term Transportation Bill
417.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the importance of moving forward on a long-term transportation bill. She specifically referenced the recent I-10 bridge collapse in California. The bill would provide three years of guaranteed funding and six years of program authorization.

418.title: Boxer and Hatch Emphasize Need for Bipartisan Cooperation To Pass Long-Term Transportation Bill
418.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the need for bipartisan cooperation to pass a long-term transportation bill and the importance of rebuilding America's infrastructure. The bill would provide three years of guaranteed funding and six years of program authorization.

419.title: Boxer, Senate Colleagues and DOT Secretary Foxx Urge Republicans for a Long-term Transportation Bill
419.description: Senate Democrats, and Department of Transportation Secretary Anthony Foxx, called on Senate Republicans to unveil their plan for a transportation bill that could, according to news reports, be on the Senate floor for consideration next week. Without Congressional action, the Highway Trust Fund will expire on July 31st, jeopardizing the funding of critical infrastructure projects throughout the country.

420.title: Boxer, Inhofe, Vitter, Carper Introduce Six-Year Surface Transportation Reauthorization Bill
420.description: Barbara Boxer (D-CA), ranking member of the Senate EPW Committee; Sens. Jim Inhofe (R-Okla.), chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; David Vitter (R-La.), chairman of the EPW Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure; and Tom Carper (D-Del.), senior member of the EPW Committee, today introduced a six-year surface transportation reauthorization bill titled the Developing a Reliable and Innovative Vision for the Economy (DRIVE) Act.

421.title: Boxer Speaks on Senate Floor About the Urgent Need to Pass a Long-Term Transportation Bill
421.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor today about the immediate need for Congress to pass a long-term transportation bill.

422.title: Senator Boxer's Opening Statement: Full EPW Committee Markup
422.description: The Senate Environment and Public Works Committee held a full committee business meeting to consider S. 697, Frank. R. Lautenberg Chemical Security for the 21st Century Act, S. 544, Secret Science Reform Act, and GSA Resolutions.

423.title: Senator Boxer and Public Health Leaders, including Deirdre Imus, Call for Reform of TSCA
423.description:
Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), will be joined by public health leaders, including Deirdre Imus, a children’s health advocate, to discuss the need for toxic chemical reform that will protect public health.  

Last month, Deirdre Imus, a contributor to Fox News, came out in opposition to S. 697, the Udall-Vitter toxic chemicals bill for failing to protect families from toxic chemicals. 

 In the op-ed, she stated: “For those of us who have been screaming at the top of our lungs for someone, anyone to listen about the dangers chemicals pose to human health, this proposed law feels like a punch in the gut.”

424.title: Senators Boxer, Inhofe, and Job Creators Call for Action on Transportation Bill
424.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, and James Inhofe (R-OK), Chairman, were joined by a broad coalition of businesses, labor, and transportation organizations to emphasize the importance of a long-term surface transportation bill and the need for Congress to act. The latest extension of the current transportation law, the Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act (MAP-21), expires on May 31, 2015.

425.title: Senator Boxer Speaks In Opposition to Udall-Vitter TSCA Bill
425.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, gave an opening statement at the March 18th legislative hearing on chemical safety. Text of her remarks can be found here: http://1.usa.gov/1BMBIZq

426.title: Senators Boxer and Markey Hold Press Conference Calling for a Toxic Chemicals Reform Bill
426.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), and Senator Edward J. Markey (D-MA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Superfund, Waste Management, and Regulatory Oversight, held a press conference on the urgent need to pass a toxic chemical reform bill that is stronger than current law to protect children and communities from the dangers of toxins. On March 12th, Senators Boxer and Markey introduced the Alan Reinstein and Trevor Schaefer Toxic Chemical Protection Act as an alternative to the Udall-Vitter-Inhofe toxics bill. The Boxer-Markey bill is named after Alan Reinstein, who passed away in 2006 at the age of 66 from mesothelioma, a disease often associated with exposure to asbestos.  Alan and his wife, Linda, cofounded the Asbestos Disease Awareness Organization (ADAO) in 2004. The legislation is also named after Trevor Schaefer, a brain cancer survivor who was diagnosed with the disease twelve years ago at the age of 13.

427.title: Senator Boxer speaks in opposition to new Committee policy on banning opening statements
427.description: Senator Boxer expresses her opposition to new EPW Committee policy banning members, except for the Chairman and Ranking Member, from delivering opening statements at Committee hearings.

428.title: Boxer Presents Gavel to Inhofe and Urges Quick Action on Transportation Bill
428.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member, turned over the gavel to Chairman Inhofe during EPW’s first business meeting this morning and urged quick action on a transportation bill.

429.title: Senator Boxer's Floor Statement Against Keystone XL
429.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor in opposition to S. 1, a bill to approve the Keystone tar sands pipeline.

430.title: Senator Boxer gives closing remarks in opposition to the Keystone XL Pipeline
430.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, gives remarks prior to the Senate’s defeat of S. 2280, a bill that would have forced the approval of the Keystone tar sands pipeline.

431.title: Senator Boxer's Speaks Out Against Keystone XL Pipeline
431.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor in opposition to S. 2280, a bill to approve the Keystone tar sands pipeline.

432.title: Senators Boxer, Cardin, Sanders, & Murphy Tout Benefits of EPA Standards to Address Climate Change
432.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD), Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT), and Senator Chris Murphy (D-CT) held a press conference to highlight the important role that the Environmental Protection Agency’s proposed carbon pollution standards for existing power plants will have on reducing dangerous air pollution, protecting the health of children and families, and creating clean energy jobs.

433.title: Senator Boxer speaks on the need to find a long-term fix for the Highway Trust Fund
433.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), spoke on the floor about the need to find a long-term solution to fund the Highway Trust Fund before the end of the year. In May, the EPW Committee unanimously passed a long-term bipartisan bill to reauthorize the nation's transportation programs for six years at current levels plus inflation. (7/21/14)

434.title: Boxer and Transportation Leaders Press Conference to Signal HTF Facing a Mayday Situation
434.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), along with transportation stakeholders, held a press conference to underscore the urgent need for Congress to address the looming short-term and long-term funding crisis in the Highway Trust Fund. In May, the EPW Committee unanimously passed a long term bill to reauthorize the nation's surface transportation programs for six years at current funding levels plus inflation.

435.title: President Obama Signs Water Resource Reform & Development Act (WRRDA)
435.description: President Obama signed the Water Resources Reform and Development Act (WRRDA) into law.  Senator Boxer served as the chair of the Senate-House, bipartisan conference on the legislation.  The conference report, which passed overwhelmingly in the House (412-4) and the Senate (91-7) in May, contains many of the top priorities and new initiatives from the Senate-passed bill, including reforms to the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund, a focus on addressing extreme weather, and a new funding mechanism, the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA), that will assist localities in need of resources for flood control, wastewater or drinking water infrastructure (June 10, 2014).

436.title: Boxer Addresses Climate Change Denier Claims
436.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA) and members of the Senate Climate Action Task Force invited Republican Senators to the Senate floor to discuss climate solutions (June 9, 2014).

437.title: Wake Up Congress for Climate Action Event (May 21, 2014)
437.description: Speakers included members of the Senate Climate Action Task Force, the Bicameral Climate Change Task Force, the House Safe Climate Caucus, and the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition, as well as House and Senate leadership. Participants both at the event and across the country were encouraged to "sound the alarm" on climate change at 5 pm ET on cell phones, tablets or hand held devices. The event followed an all-night session in March, where 31 Senators took to the floor to "wake up" Congress on the need to act now to address the growing threat of climate change.

438.title: Senator Boxer and Colleagues Make Major Announcement on Transportation Reauthorization Bill
438.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, Senator David Vitter (R-LA), Ranking Member of the Committee, Senator Tom Carper (D-DE), Chairman of the Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee, and Senator John Barrasso (R-WY), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee, today made a major announcement regarding the reauthorization of the transportation bill, entitled Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).

439.title: Boxer Joins Nurses to Spotlight Harmful Health Impacts of Tar Sands and Keystone XL Pipeline
439.description:
Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), held a press conference Thursday, March 13th with nurses from across the United States to describe the harmful health implications associated with tar sands oil and the proposed Keystone XL pipeline, as well as their plans for further action. On February 26th, Senators Boxer and Whitehouse (D-RI) called on Secretary of State John Kerry and the Obama Administration to analyze the public health risks to communities from the proposed Keystone pipeline.

Senator Boxer was joined by nurses from hospitals in areas affected by tar sands and the proposed pipeline, who described the health symptoms experienced by their patients and their plans for future actions.

Nurses that spoke included:

Karen Higgins, RN, National Nurses United Co-President, Boston, Massachusetts 
Kari Columbus, RN Kansas City, Kansas
Rolanda Watson, RN, Chicago, Illinois 
Brenda Prewitt, RN, Houston, Texas 
Katy Roemer, RN, Oakland, California

440.title: Senators Boxer, Whitehouse Expose Harmful Health Impacts of Tar Sands and Keystone XL Pipeline
440.description:
Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), and Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) held a press conference on Wednesday, February 26th to expose the harmful health implications associated with tar sands oil and the proposed Keystone XL pipeline, which is currently under consideration. Senators Boxer, Whitehouse, doctors and community representatives spoke about the health impacts of tar sands oil on communities across the country.  Additional speakers included:

Dr. John O'Connor, MD, Alberta, Canada

Dr. Stuart Batterman, Professor of Environmental Health Sciences, Univ. of Michigan School of Public Health 

Hilton Kelley, Founder and CEO, Community In-power & Development Association Inc., Port Arthur, TX

Tom Shepherd, Vice President, Southeast Environmental Task Force, Chicago, IL

441.title: Senator Boxer's Statement at Hearing on the Chemical Spill near Charleston, WV (Feb. 4, 2014)
441.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, gave an opening statement at a February 4th Subcommittee on Water and Wildlife hearing examining the safety and security of drinking water supplies following the Central West Virginia drinking water crisis.  Text of her remarks can be found here: http://1.usa.gov/1eQK7jQ

442.title: Boxer Speaks Out Against Proposed Keystone XL Pipeline Amendment to Senate Energy Bill (9/12/13)
442.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke out on the Senate floor against a proposed amendment supporting the construction Keystone XL pipeline as part of the Shaheen-Portman energy bill (9/12/13)

443.title: Boxer, Whitehouse, and Senate Colleagues Kick Off Initiative to Wake Up Congress on Climate Change
443.description: During a press conference today, Senators Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), announced the members of a newly formed Senate Climate Action Task Force and discussed their plans to take action on climate change.

444.title: Senator Boxer's Message on the UN Climate Change Conference in Warsaw, Poland (November 21, 2013)
444.description: Text of Senator Boxer's remarks can be found here: http://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm?FuseAction=Majority.PressReleases&ContentRecord_id=7bdd3253-c4c8-b794-d9fa-8b5ebafbf089

445.title: Sens. Boxer, Cardin and Hirono highlight damaging impacts of Government Shutdown (October 16, 2013)
445.description:
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD), Chairman of the EPW Subcommittee on Water and Wildlife, and Senator Mazie Hirono (D-HI) were joined by a business owner, industry leaders and community representatives to discuss how the government shutdown is impacting local economies, families and communities nationwide.  The speakers highlighted how the shutdown is delaying putting people to work repairing aging infrastructure in projects authorized in the Water Resources Development Act, as well as impeding the clean-up actions needed to protect families living near Superfund toxic waste sites, creating economic losses to local businesses that rely heavily on outdoor recreation, and stopping the creation of critically important worker safety protections at dangerous chemical facilities.  The list of speakers included:

-Stephen Sandherr, Chief Executive Officer, Associated General Contractors of America

-Susan Meredith, co-owner of Blackwater Pedal and Paddle Adventures, Dorchester County, Maryland

-Kirk Bailey, Vice President of Government Affairs, Outdoor Industry Association

-Stephen Lester, Science Director at the Center for Health, Environment & Justice, and 

-Anna Fendley, Legislative Representative, United Steel Workers

446.title: Sens. Boxer, Cardin & Nelson Highlight Damaging Impacts of Government Shutdown (October 8, 2013)
446.description:
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD), Chairman of the EPW Subcommittee on Water and Wildlife, and Senator Bill Nelson (D-FL) were joined by representatives from several organizations today to highlight how families and communities are being impacted by the shutdown of the federal government.  The speakers discussed how critical services, including the cleanup of toxic waste sites, the operation of wildlife refuges, investment in the transportation sector, and the investigation and prevention of chemical explosions and disasters, are being negatively affected by the shutdown.  

Speakers joining the senators included: 
-Debbie Mans, Executive Director, New York / New Jersey Baykeeper
-Dr. Rafael Moure-Eraso, Chairman, U.S. Chemical Safety Board
-Birgit P. Vertesch, Executive Director, "Ding" Darling Wildlife Society; Sanibel Island, FL                           
-Dr. T. Peter Ruane, President and CEO, American Road and Transportation Builders Association

447.title: Boxer Speaks Out in Opposition to Keystone XL Pipeline Amendment to Senate Energy Bill
447.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke out on the Senate floor against an amendment that supports the construction of the Keystone XL pipeline as part of the Shaheen-Portman energy bill (9/12/13).

448.title: Boxer Highlights Urgent Need to Protect 3 Million Transportation-Related Jobs (July 25, 2013)
448.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, along with transportation stakeholders, held a press conference to highlight the need to protect 3 million transportation-related jobs, which are at risk due to severe funding shortfalls projected after the expiration of the transportation law, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act (MAP-21), in September 2014.

449.title: Ceremony Naming the EPA Headquarters Building in Honor of President Bill Clinton (July 17, 2013)
449.description:
July 17, 2013 - Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), joined President Bill Clinton at a ceremony to mark the naming of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) headquarters in Washington, DC in his honor.  President Clinton gave remarks, as well as Senator Boxer and former EPA Administrator Carol Browner.

The EPW Committee passed the legislation naming the EPA Headquarters after President Clinton in December 2012: http://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm?FuseAction=PressRoom.PressReleases&ContentRecord_id=B9D3E38E-9448-209C-317B-86F00308B15F

Video is courtesy of EPA and can also be found here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lRuA735LkQ8

450.title: Boxer Asks Governors to Review and Adopt Policies to Help Prevent Chemical Explosions (7/9/13)
450.description: Washington, D.C. -- Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), held a press conference today to call for action following the West, Texas chemical explosion in April.  For more information, please visit: http://goo.gl/2T5a3

451.title: Boxer Presses NRC Chair on Safety Review of San Onofre Nuclear Power Plant (May 23, 2013)
451.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), today pressed Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Chairman Allison Macfarlane on the NRC's ongoing safety review and investigations of California's San Onofre nuclear power plant. The San Onofre nuclear power plant, which is located in a seismic and tsunami zone, has been shut down since January 2012 after a leak of radioactive material led to the discovery of unexpected deterioration of tubes in the plant's new steam generators.  The EPW Committee met to consider Macfarlane's renomination as NRC Chairman.  A full webcast of the hearing can be found here: http://www.senate.gov/isvp/?type=live&comm=epw&filename=epw052313

452.title: Boxer Begins Senate Floor Debate on the Water Resources Development Act (May 7, 2013)
452.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor to begin debate on S.601, the Water Resources Development Act of 2013 (WRDA).  The bill, which passed the EPW Committee unanimously in March, would provide critical flood protection, environmental restoration projects, and investment in ports and wastewater and drinking water infrastructure.    Boxer cosponsored the bill with EPW Ranking Member David Vitter (R-LA).

453.title: Senator Boxer Praises Credentials of EPA Nominee Gina McCarthy (April 11, 2013)
453.description:
Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, delivers her opening statement at a hearing to consider the nomination of Gina McCarthy to be Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).  McCarthy currently serves as the Assistant Administrator for EPA's Office of Air and Radiation.

Read Senator Boxer's statement here: http://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm?FuseAction=Majority.PressReleases&ContentRecord_id=f9a20b93-e3a9-0b34-93dc-b0ff01545fd7

454.title: Boxer Praises EPA Nominee Gina McCarthy in her closing remarks at EPW Hearing (April 11, 2013)
454.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, provides some closing remarks at a hearing to consider the nomination of Gina McCarthy to be Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).  McCarthy currently serves as the Assistant Administrator for EPA's Office of Air and Radiation.

455.title: Boxer Speaks on the Need for U.S. Leadership to Address Climate Disruption (April 8, 2013)
455.description:
Senator Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, spoke on the Senate floor about the need for U.S. leadership to address climate disruption.

The speech is one in a series as Sen. Boxer discusses the threat of climate change and the steps that can be taken to avoid climate disruption's devastating effects.

456.description:
Senator Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, spoke on the Senate floor about the dangerous impacts of climate disruption on public health.  

The speech is one in a series as Sen. Boxer discusses the threat of climate change and the steps that can be taken to avoid climate disruption's devastating effects.  Video from Sen. Boxer's previous climate floor speeches can be found below:

457.title: Boxer Continues Weekly Floor Series on the Impacts of Climate Disruption (March 11, 2013)
457.description:
Senator Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, spoke on the Senate floor about the impacts of dangerous climate change and climate disruption.  Sen. Boxer discussed a recent report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO), which added climate change to its 2013 High Risk List.  She also referred to a recent study in Science stating that average global temperatures were higher in the past decade than over most of the previous 11,300 years. 

http://www.gao.gov/highrisk/limiting_federal_government_fiscal_exposure

The speech is one in a series as Sen. Boxer discusses the threat of climate change and the steps that can be taken to avoid climate disruption's devastating effects.  Video from Sen. Boxer's previous climate floor speech, on March 4, 2013, can be found here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h70RMdwb7jU&feature=youtu.be

458.title: Senator Boxer Speaks on the Impacts of Climate Change (March 4, 2013)
458.description:
Senator Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, spoke on the Senate floor about the impacts of dangerous climate change: http://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2013/02/28/climate-change-remaking-america/1917169/.

The speech is one in a series as Sen. Boxer discusses the threat of climate change and the steps that can be taken to avoid climate disruption's devastating effects.

459.title: Chairman Boxer & Senator Sanders Introduce Major Climate Change Legislation (Feb. 14)
459.description:
Senator Barbara Boxer (D-Calif.), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), and Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT), held a news conference to announce comprehensive legislation, the Climate Protection Act (S. 332). Senator Sanders serves on the EPW Committee and also is a member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

S. 332 calls for a fee on carbon pollution emissions that would fund historic investments in energy efficiency and sustainable energy technologies, such as wind, solar, geothermal, and biomass. The proposal also provides rebates to consumers to offset any efforts by oil, coal, or gas companies to raise prices.

Environment and consumer leaders that participated in the press conference included Bill McKibben, founder of 350.org; Mike Brune, executive director of Sierra Club; Tara McGuiness, executive director of the Center for American Progress Action Fund; Tyson Slocum, Public Citizen's energy director; and David Bradley, National Community Action Foundation executive director.

460.title: Senator Boxer's Message on the UN Climate Conference in Doha, Qatar
460.description: Full text of Senator Boxer's remarks can be found here: http://1.usa.gov/VJNC3I

461.title: Senators Boxer and Cardin Discuss Health Risks Posed to Military Personnel at Firing Ranges
461.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), and Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD), held a press conference today to announce the findings of a major scientific report from the NAS.  The report, released today, finds overwhelming evidence that the current lead exposure standards are not sufficient to adequately protect the health of military firing range personnel, and that actions must be taken to mitigate the risks (December 3, 2012).

462.title: President Obama Signs Transportation Reauthorization Bill into Law (July 6, 2012)
462.description: President Barack Obama signs the transportation reauthorization bill into law. Senator Boxer (D-CA) served as the chair of the House-Senate, bipartisan conference on the transportation legislation. The bill, part of a legislative package that includes provisions related to student loans and flood insurance, passed both the Senate and House of Representatives on June 29 with overwhelming bipartisan support and keeps funding at current levels through 2014. Video courtesy of www.whitehouse.gov

463.title: Boxer Praises Senate Passage of Transportation Reauthorization Conference Report (June 29, 2012)
463.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, applauded the Senate's 74-19 passage of the surface transportation bill conference report. The report is a bipartisan, bicameral agreement to fund surface transportation programs through the end of FY 2014, and culminates months of work between conferees to resolve differences between the House and Senate versions of the bill.  The House of Representatives also overwhelmingly passed the measure, 373-52  The legislative package, which also includes provisions related to student loans and flood insurance, will now go to the President to be signed into law (June 29, 2012).

464.title: Senator Boxer Provides Remarks on House-Senate Transportation Conference Agreement (June 28, 2012)
464.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, today spoke on the Senate floor regarding the House-Senate transportation bill conference report.  Senator Boxer yesterday announced a bipartisan, bicameral agreement to fund surface transportation programs through 2014 (June 28, 2012).

465.title: Boxer Speaks Against Attempt to roll-back EPA's Clean Air Rule for Power Plants (June 20, 2012)
465.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke against a Senate Republican proposal to prevent the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) from implementing clean air standards for lead, arsenic and other toxics for power plants. The measure was defeated, 46-53 (June 20, 2012).

466.title: Boxer & Senate Colleagues Hold Rally Highlighting Urgent Need to Pass Transportation Bill (6/13/12)
466.description:
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, and Senate colleagues held a rally in front of the U.S. Capitol to urge the House-Senate Transportation Conference Committee to pass a conference report reauthorizing the nation's surface transportation programs before they expire on June 30.  The Senators were joined by job creators, including representatives from the construction industry and transportation sector, which have been particularly hard hit by the delay in passing a transportation bill.  During the rally, a convoy of heavy trucks used in road construction drove by the Capitol in support of passing the transportation bill by June 30.

Joining Boxer were Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Mark Begich (D-AK), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Mary Landrieu (D-LA), John Kerry (D-MA), Christopher Coons (D-DE), and Richard Blumenthal (D-DE), as well as Jack Basso, Chief Operating Officer of the American Association of Highway and Transit Officials (AASHTO), and Bill Childs, President and CEO of Chaney Enterprises and Vice Chairman of the National Ready Mixed Concrete Association (NRMCA).

467.title: Sen. Boxer Provides Update on Transportation Bill Conference (May 23, 2012)
467.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), held a press briefing with Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) to provide an update on the House and Senate conference on the surface transportation bill. Senator Boxer, who serves as Chairman of the conference, convened the opening meeting on May 8th. The current transportation authorization expires on June 30, 2012.

468.title: Boxer Remarks at House-Senate Conference Opening Meeting on Transportation Bill (May 8, 2012)
468.description:
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW) (Conference Chairman) addressed conferees at the opening meeting. 

Senator Boxer and Senator James Inhofe (R-OK), Ranking Member of the Committee, worked together with their EPW Committee colleagues to develop a two-year surface transportation bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21), which maintains funding at current levels.  On March 14, 2012, the Senate passed the bill with overwhelming bipartisan support, 74-22.  The current transportation authorization expires on June 30, 2012.

469.title: Senator Boxer Responds to Vote on 90-Day Stop Gap Extension of Transportation Programs (3/29/12)
469.description: Senator Barbara Boxer, Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, commented on Senate action this afternoon to pass the House of Representatives' 90-day stop gap extension of transportation programs before the March 31st deadline.  Boxer has worked with her Senate colleagues to pass a bipartisan two year bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21), and vowed to keep the pressure on House Republicans to pass a bipartisan transportation bill.

470.title: Boxer & Cardin Highlight Urgent Need for Action on Bipartisan Senate Transportation Bill (3/29/12)
470.description: Senator Barbara Boxer, Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, and Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD), a member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee, held a press conference to discuss the serious economic damages in states across the country that would be caused by the failure of the House of Representatives to pass the bipartisan Senate transportation bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).  Without the funding stability provided by the Senate's bipartisan transportation bill, many projects to fix our nation's crumbling infrastructure -- including the nearly 70,000 structurally deficient bridges -- will be deferred.  Short-term stop gap extensions also pose a threat to such projects and the jobs they support.

471.title: Boxer, Schumer, & Begich urge House to Pass Bipartisan Senate Transportation bill (March 28, 2012)
471.description: Today, Senator Barbara Boxer, Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, held a press conference with Senators Charles Schumer (D-NY) and Mark Begich (D-AK) to discuss the serious economic damages in states across the country that would be caused by the failure of the House of Representatives to pass the bipartisan Senate transportation bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21). The current transportation authorization is set to expire on March 31st, and transportation programs across the nation will shut down without congressional action.

472.title: Senators join Boxer & DOT Sec. LaHood call to House: Pass Bipartisan Transportation Bill (3/21/12)
472.description:
At a press conference held this morning on Capitol Hill, Senator Boxer and Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood were joined by Senators Charles Schumer (D-NY), Ben Cardin (D-MD), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Mark Begich (D-AK) to urge House Leadership to drop a proposed short-term extension and instead pass the Senate's bipartisan legislation, which will save 1.9 million jobs and up to an additional one million jobs by leveraging federal funding.
.

473.title: Boxer and DOT Sec. LaHood call on House to Pass Bipartisan Senate Transportation Bill (3/21/12)
473.description:
At a press conference held this morning on Capitol Hill, Senator Boxer and Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood urged House Leadership to drop a proposed short-term extension and instead pass the Senate's bipartisan legislation, which will save 1.9 million jobs and up to an additional one million jobs by leveraging federal funding.

Note: Video is of excerpts to the press conference.  Video of the full press conference can be found here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UM5fSC4WkmI

474.title: Boxer Applauds Senate Bipartisan Passage of Transportation Bill (March 14, 2012)
474.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), today praised the Senate's passage of the bipartisan surface transportation bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).  The bill passed the Senate today by a 74-22 vote.  Senator Boxer thanked her colleagues on both sides of the aisle for their cooperation and compromise in crafting the bipartisan legislation, which reauthorizes the nation's surface transportation programs for two years.  Current funding for surface transportation programs expires March 31, 2012, and Senator Boxer urged the House to pass the Senate bill before the current extension expires.

475.title: Boxer Denounces Distraction, Urges Colleagues to Move Forward on Transportation Bill (Feb. 28, 2012)
475.description:
U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), chairman of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), underscored the importance of passing the Senate's bipartisan transportation reauthorization bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).  Boxer denounced an unrelated birth-control amendment to the bill that is pending consideration.  

Senators Boxer and Committee Ranking Member James Inhofe (R-OK) worked together with their EPW Committee colleagues to develop MAP-21, which maintains funding at current levels. The bipartisan measure passed unanimously in the EPW Committee on November 9, 2011. The current transportation authorization expires on March 31, 2012.

476.title: Boxer Urges Colleagues to Pass Much-Needed Transportation Bill (February 16, 2012)
476.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works, urged Senate colleagues to drop unrelated provisions on a much-needed transportation reauthorization bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).  The Senate voted 85-11 on February 10 to proceed to debate on the bill.  Senators Boxer and Committee Ranking Member James Inhofe (R-OK) worked together with their EPW Committee colleagues to develop this legislation, which maintains funding at current levels. The bipartisan measure passed unanimously in the EPW Committee on November 9, 2011. The current transportation authorization expires on March 31, 2012.

477.title: Boxer's Opening Floor Remarks on EPW's Transportation Bill, MAP-21 (February 9, 2012)
477.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, spoke on the Senate floor in support of the Committee's two-year surface transportation bill, Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21).  The Senate later voted to proceed with debate on the bill. The final vote was 85-11.   Senators Boxer and Committee Ranking Member James Inhofe (R-OK) worked together with their EPW Committee colleagues to develop this legislation, which maintains funding at current levels.  The bipartisan measure passed unanimously in the EPW Committee on November 9, 2011. The current transportation authorization expires on March 31, 2012.

478.title: Boxer Discusses Progress on a Surface Transportation Bill This Year (Jan. 26, 2012)
478.description: Senator Barbara Boxer, Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, held a press conference to discuss the progress on a surface transportation bill this year. Senator Boxer and her Senate colleagues have developed a bipartisan bill - Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century (MAP-21) - which would reauthorize the nation's surface transportation programs for the next two years. This bipartisan proposal passed unanimously through the EPW Committee on November 9, 2011, and is awaiting consideration by the full Senate. The current surface transportation authorization is set to expire on March 31, 2012.

479.title: Boxer Opening Statement at EPW hearing on NRC recommendations for reactor safety (December 15, 2011)
479.description: Opening statement of Senate Environment and Public Works Committee Chairman Barbara Boxer (D-CA) at Full and Subcommittee on Clean Air and Nuclear Safety joint hearing entitled, "Review of the NRC's Near-Term Task Force Recommendations for Enhancing Reactor Safety in the 21st Century" (December 15, 2011)

480.title: Boxer and Colleagues Speak Against Dangerous House Riders to Must-Pass Legislation (Dec. 12, 2011)
480.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, joined Senators Tom Carper (D-DE), Frank Lautenberg (D-NJ), Ben Cardin (D-MD) and representatives from leading environmental and public health organizations to discuss dangerous provisions that Republicans have attached to must-pass payroll and appropriations legislation. Senator Boxer and other members of the EPW Committee oppose the Republican-supported provisions in the year-end legislation because they will harm the environment and public health (December 13, 2011).

481.title: Senator Boxer Sends Message on Climate Change to the Durban Conference (Dec 7, 2011)
481.description: As the United Nations climate change conference continues in Durban, South Africa, Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, held a press conference to discuss climate change and the need for international cooperation.  She also addressed claims made by climate change deniers (Dec. 7, 2011).

482.title: Boxer speaks against attacks to the Cross State Air Pollution rule (November 10, 2011)
482.description: Senator Boxer speaks against S.J.Res27, a resolution that would  have eliminated the Cross State Air Pollution rule and clean air safeguards.  The measure failed by a 41-56 vote (November 10, 2011).

483.title: Boxer Speaks on the Floor in Opposition to Republican Efforts to Block President Obama's Jobs Bill
483.description: Senator Boxer speaks on the Floor in opposition to Republican efforts to block President Obama's proposal that would create jobs and invest in infrastructure (November 3, 2011).

484.title: Senator Boxer Speaks on the Importance of Transportation Enhancement Funding (Oct. 19, 2011)
484.description: Senator Boxer spoke on the Senate floor before the Senate voted against a McCain amendment that would have eliminated several activities under the Transportation Enhancements (TE) program and prohibited states from using any Federal transportation funds for these activities.  By a vote of 59 to 39, the McCain amendment was tabled (October 19, 2011).

485.title: Chairman Boxer Releases a New Report to Address Attacks on EPA (October 6, 2011)
485.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, released an EPW Committee Majority Staff Report that sets the record straight about the essential contributions that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and landmark environmental laws have made in protecting public health and promoting economic growth. Senator Boxer was joined at the press conference by Senator Ben Cardin (D-MD) and representatives from several organizations that represent families and workers, including the United Auto Workers (UAW) and the American Lung Association.  The report was prepared to refute the continuing attacks on environmental protections by House Republicans. The House of Representatives is considering legislation this week to weaken EPA's authority to regulate toxic emissions.

486.title: Senator Boxer Press Conference on Defending the Clean Air Act (September 21, 2011)
486.description: Senators Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, Frank Lautenberg (D-NJ) and Ben Cardin (D-MD) were joined by public health experts from the American Lung Association, Physicians for Social Responsibility and a family that has been affected by asthma to discuss the need to protect  the Clean Air Act and the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) role in safeguarding families and communities. The House of Representatives has considered legislation that would have devastating impacts on the health of children and families nationwide.  Today, President Obama threatened to veto the latest assault on clean air protections (September 21, 2011).

487.title: Sen. Boxer statement on the need to pass Transportation & FAA Extension (9/15/11)
487.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer, Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works, speaks against Republican holds on the Transportation Extension, FAA & FEMA funding and highlights the jobs at risk (September 15, 2011).

488.title: Sen. Boxer's opening statement at EPW's hearing on the draft transportation bill (July 21, 2011)
488.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW), provides an opening statement at the July 21, 2011 Full Committee hearing entitled, "Legislative Issues for Transportation Reauthorization."

489.title: Chairman Boxer Press Conference on Transportation Bill (July 6, 2011)
489.description: Senator Barbara Boxer (D-CA), Chairman of the Environment and Public Works Committee, held a press conference today and released new numbers regarding transportation-related job losses nationwide under the House passed budget plan.  For further details, visit: http://1.usa.gov/pA6Joj

490.title: Sen. Boxer discusses Republicans blocking EDA Bill with MSNBC's Lawrence O'Donnell (June 21, 2011)
490.description: U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer appeared on MSNBC's The Last Word with Lawrence O'Donnell to discuss Senate Republicans blocking S.782, the Economic Development Administration (EDA) Bill and other job-creating bills.

491.title: Senator Boxer Speaks in Support of EDA Authorization, S.782 (June 16, 2011)
491.description: In a Floor Statement June 16, 2011, Senator Boxer highlights the job-creation opportunities of S.782 and describes Republican attempts to filibuster the bill using amendments.

492.title: Boxer Opening Statement for Committee Hearing on NRC Review of Nuclear Plant Safety in the U.S.
492.description: U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW) Chairman Barbara Boxer's opening remarks at the June 16, 2011 EPW hearing on U.S. Nuclear Plant Safety.

493.title: Boxer  Opening Statement for Full Committee Hearing: The Clean Air Act and Public Health
493.description: U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee (EPW) Chairman Barbara Boxer speaks on the importance of the Clean Air Act in protecting public health at an EPW hearing, June 15, 2011.

494.title: Sen. Boxer June 7 floor speech supporting EDA Reauthorization
494.description: Senator Boxer speaks on the Floor in support of passage of S.782, the Economic Development Revitalization Act of 2011,  which provides investments in infrastructure and job creation efforts to economically distressed communities.

495.title: EPW Chairman Boxer meets with 6th grade students from Mecca Elementary School on Capitol Hill
495.description: Chairman Boxer meet with 6th graders from Mecca, CA, to discuss the harmful air pollution the community has experienced (May 24, 2011).

496.title: Chairman Boxer speaks on the Senate floor April 6 against attempts to undermine the Clean Air Act
496.description: Chairman Boxer's Floor Statement prior to a Senate vote on four proposals that would interfere with the implementation of the Clean Air Act and block the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) from doing its job of curbing carbon pollution from the nation's largest polluters (April 6, 2011)

497.title: March 30 Transportation Press Conference
497.description: Chairman Boxer joined Representative John Mica (R-FL), Chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, US Chamber of Commerce President, Tom Donohue, Mayor of Los Angeles, Antonio Villaraigosa, AFL-CIO President, Richard Trumka, and the Mayor of Mesa, Arizona, Scott Smith, to stand together in support of the upcoming transportation bill (March 30, 2011).

498.title: Boxer appears on MSNBC's "The Last Word" with Lawrence O'Donnell on nuclear crisis, March 16, 2011
498.description: Chairman Boxer appears on MSNBC's "The Last Word" with Lawrence O'Donnell to discuss the nuclear crisis in Japan and its implications for the U.S. (March 16, 2011).

499.title: Chaiman Boxer's Exchange with NRC Chair Gregory Jaczko at March 16 EPW NRC briefing
499.description: Chairman Boxer questions U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) Chairman Gregory Jazcko at a March 16 Committee briefing on the Nuclear Disaster in Japan and Implications for the United States.

500.title: March 3, 2011 Boxer Floor Remarks on attacks to Clean Air Act
500.description: Chairman Boxer speaks on the floor of the U.S. Senate regarding the impact of the House Republican budget (H.R.1) on public health and the Environmental Protection Agency (March 3, 2011).
